full_judgment: 10. In the decision reported in 46 DLR 267, the defendant filed an application praying for settling the issues of law, namely, the issues on maintainability of the suit on the grounds of limitation, bar under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, res judicata and also defect of parties and the Assistant Judge after hearing the application by the impugned order only took up the question of res judicata and held that the other issues cannot be decided without hearing the suit on merit. Before the High Court question was raised as to whether the provision of rule 2 of Order 14, CPC is mandatory and the court at first is to decide the issue on limitation as it is incumbent upon the court to determine the issue of law at first as it saves unnecessary expense, time and labour of the court itself. It was held by the High Court Division that the failure to decide the issue on limitation on the face of Order 14 rule 2 CPC is an error of law on the part of the court and contrary to the decision consistently followed by the superior courts and the provision of Order 14 rule 2 CPC is mandatory and the trial Court is under mandate of law to decide the issue of law where an application under Order 14 rule 2 CPC is filed by the party to the suit.
